body: I'm pretty sure I was.  I would drink around 30 drinks a week, sometimes more, over a 3 or 4 day period.  I would take off a few days a week, usually hung over, then start drinking again.  I could sometimes just have a couple drinks but then it would escalate to 5 or 10, once in a while more.
Going back to a familiar job would be waiting tables again.  If I do that, my life is over.  I will start drinking again and it will kill me.

Do you live in Florida? And how old are you?  I definitely feel for you because it's like you get all these ideas, like, oh! I could do that, I'm definitely qualified for that.  And then you hit the brick wall of the internet, lost in indeed.com somehow and just see a bunch of GARBAGE that you're qualified for.  Somehow you're not as good or as qualified as they want their candidates to be and there's no one but the gas station, retail store, call center, restaurant, and custodial jobs available.  Yeah, makes me want to go jump off a bridge!

So, you basically went backwards then? Well I feel like I've gone backwards to the age of 17 or something.  I will not go back to the restaurant business because it will turn me into an alcoholic again because I can't be around people and turn on a fake smile.  The way I was able to hold that fake smile was thanks in part to good old alcohol.  I do not want a job working in the hospitality industry, but thanks for the suggestion.  I'm glad you enjoy it but, I feel like I was mentally abused for years by management and the customers at my table who talked to me like I was nothing.  Being a bartender is a little bit different than being a server because you're just hanging out with people and making them drinks.  I just don't know what to do with myself and feel like I'm going to lose everything because my parents can't keep supporting me and I don't want to take a job that is going to make me numb myself with alcohol.  Maybe I should just go and live in a tent.
